summary: Computer environment core: ComputerEnvironment (EnvironmentAdapter over registered modality executors with grant verification, per-primitive checks, staleness, at-most-once, serialised writes, verification, events, outcomes, accounting, execution log, restart recovery), ExecRPC v1 service + RemoteEnvironment/RemotePolicy, structured browser on Playwright Chromium (persistent / research / CDP sessions, screen() for visual control), unified perception, internal executor, five local staging sites, adapter guide. 66 tests: 43 in the default suite (no Chromium), 23 gated by the browser/privileged markers, of which 22 launch real Chromium (the 2 privileged tests additionally need root and the cambrowser user). Everything runs against local staging services only.

IH-01.limitations: All ten EnvironmentAdapter methods plus typed records, in process and over ExecRPC v1. Outcome measurements from the environment are unverified by design; verification is a separate service (not EB).

IH-02.limitations: Exercised only against the local staging sites; no public website was contacted and live operation stays blocked until the operator authorizes it. Elements inside iframes / closed shadow roots are not listed. A redirect hop is checked after it happened (tab reset to about:blank on refusal).

IH-12.limitations: The contract kit is run here against two adapters (ComputerEnvironment and the diagnostic LabWorld); no third-party harness was plugged in.

not_done: No public website and no live service was contacted; every result is a staging result. Live operation is blocked until the operator supplies authorization and credentials.

The environment was not composed with the EC (sandbox, jobs, visual) or ES (api, skill, publishing, discord) executors; that wiring (service --executor flags / build_environment) is integration work. One cross-workstream check exists: the environment against harness.auth.PolicyService in process.
RemotePolicy was tested against a small real PolicyEngine served over harness.rpc, not against the harness.auth service process.
The executor-side secret handle is not constructed by the service unless a --secrets factory is given; EB tests use a two-method broker object, not the vault.

Uid-separated Chromium is not active by default on this machine (Playwright's Chromium under /root is unreachable for cambrowser); it needs BrowserConfig.executable_path pointing at a shared install. Tested only with a temporary copy.
Structured observations do not descend into iframes or closed shadow roots.
Redirect hops are authorized after the fact (final URL), not before each hop; same-origin subresource requests are not individually checked; no kernel-level network filtering.
Research sessions block every non-GET request, so POST-based search forms do not work there.
Headed (non-headless) mode was not run; no desktop-level screenshots (viewport only).
ComputerEnvironment enforces only coarse limits (external action count, money estimate, compute, duration); rate and spending policy belong to the authorization service.
Log, journal and event-stream files are append-only without rotation or compaction.
Who calls PolicyEngine.record is unresolved in the contract (change request 3); the environment does it by default.
Action timeouts stop waiting and abandon the page load, but an executor that ignores ExecContext.cancel is not forcibly killed.
